April 17 declared as a public holiday in Mujibnagar
2022-04-13T20:01:12+06:00 | Star Digital Report
https://www.thedailystar.net/news/bangladesh/news/april-17-declared-public-holiday-mujibnagar-3004271

The government today announced April 17 as a public holiday in Meherpur's Mujibnagar upazila marking the historic Mujibnagar Day.

The decision was taken as part of the national programme organised by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Public Administration.

On this day (April 17), 50 years ago, the provisional government-in-exile took oath at a mango grove in Baidyanathtala, a border area in the present Meherpur district. Baidyanathtala was later named Mujibnagar.

Bangabandhu Sheikh Mujibur Rahman was declared the first president of the People's Republic of Bangladesh while vice-president Syed Nazrul Islam became the acting president in absence of Bangabandhu.

Tajuddin Ahmad was appointed the first prime minister, while Khandoker Moshtaque Ahmed, M Mansur Ali and AHM Quamaruzzaman were named cabinet members.
